# HCC · Celestial Atlas

> A single-page atlas of physics laboratories that COMPUTE. Opening the page
> gives an agent a live numerical instrument, not a document about one. Every
> number below was produced by running the thing that produced it.

This file exists because the capability was already here and nothing announced
it. An agent that knew to call `HCC_API` got real physics; an agent that merely
opened the URL was told nothing. That was measured, and this is the fix.

## Scientific workspace and static SDK

Start with `api/agent.json`. All resource paths in that descriptor resolve from the Atlas site root.
Human workspace: `agent.html`. No account or GPU is required.

- `api/agent-client.mjs`: ESM SDK, `connectAtlas(baseURL)` -> discover, search, describe, forecast, audit.
- `api/forecast-audit.schema.json`: complete input format for chronological forecast scoring.
- `atlas.audit(input)` returns MAE, RMSE, signed bias, baseline MSE skill, interval coverage and interval score, exact horizon groups, supplied provenance and replayable SHA-256 input.
- `forecast(control, delta)` returns a conditional scaling scenario, NOT a calibrated empirical prediction. Null evidence stays null. Perturbation endpoints are not confidence intervals.
- Observational labels and issue timestamps are caller declarations. Synthetic examples remain SYNTHETIC_ONLY; no automatic empirical validation is claimed.
- Fetch-only agents can inspect all JSON contracts. Browser agents can import the SDK by URL. Node 18+ agents should download the source and import the local module; Node does not import HTTPS modules by default.
- Public GitHub Pages hosts static resources, NOT the POST /mcp or /api/v1 compute endpoints. For those, run `node server/server.mjs`; default origin is http://127.0.0.1:8974. The same audit is registered as `prediction.holdout_audit`.
- The SDK does not modify the public site or grant publication credentials. Local computations need no secret credentials.

## Geometry research (verified 2026-10-02)

Open `index.html?research=1` or More → Geometry evidence. The explorer has FLRW/CPL distances, three alternative DESI DR2 compressed comparisons, a sourced reconstruction null test, scalar S³ modes, a geometric lensing kernel, and ten primary-source records linked to laboratories and all seven worlds.

- `api/research.json`: versioned source catalog, published numerical summaries and explicit scientific boundaries.
- `HCC_API.research`: live `flrw`, `audit`, `nullTest`, `scalarMode`, `lensingKernel`, `delensing`, `catalog`, `context`, `snapshot`, `open`, `close`.
- SDK named exports `flrw`, `geometryAudit`, `constantCurvatureFit`, `curvatureDiagnostic`, `scalarMode`, `lensingKernel`, `delensingResidual`, `researchCatalog`; `connectAtlas(...).research` uses the same kernels.
- Self-hosted `cosmology.geometry_audit` evaluates the same reference model without a GPU.
- DESI distance/AP alternatives overlap: never sum their χ². No topology probability is inferred. Reconstruction covariance must be full cross-redshift Cov[ΩK]; without it, significance stays null. Synthetic examples are marked.
- Closed curvature does not establish global S³ topology. Native S³ n differs from observed S² ℓ. The lensing kernel omits growth/power/bias likelihoods. No GP refit, ForestFlow emulator, Hu–Sawicki solver or complete CMB likelihood is implemented.
- Cosmological redshift/lookback never mutate the atlas J2000 clock or other world parameters. Export carries current navigation/time context, exact inputs and source catalog.

## Full Atlas runtime

Load the page and wait for the runtime:

    await HCC_API.ready({ timeout: 20000 })

Then compute. This is a real call and a real answer:

    HCC_API.evaluate('bb', { T: 5772 })
    → { radiance: 2.6239e13,
        lambda_max: 5.0204e-7,      // 502 nm — the solar peak, from Wien
        exitance: 6.2939e7,          // W/m² — from Stefan–Boltzmann
        peak_radiance: 2.6240e13,
        fraction_of_peak: 0.99996 }

Add `?render=0` to the URL to skip WebGL entirely. The physics does not need it,
and `HCC_API.capabilities()` will tell you what the browser gave you.

## The surface

    version  ready  schema  help  health  capabilities
    list     describe  evaluate        laboratories, their contracts, their answers — counts in api/manifest.json
    bus      links  wires  publishes   what is coupled to what
    bus.refusal  bus.refusals          WHY a coupling was refused, in writing
    bus.contested  bus.isolated  bus.counterfactual
    unmeasured                          what this atlas admits it has not measured
    reach  sensitivity  transfers  liveness
    stations                            sub-stations of a laboratory: .of .all .current .go
    scales  siUnits  instruments  selftest  report  markdown  ui

And beside it, the same contracts read four more ways:

    HCC_PSPACE.open(id)            any output over any two inputs as a surface; the power law
                                   it obeys (exponents as fractions); the Jacobian at a point;
                                   a phase portrait along a clock; bus doors that carry values
    HCC_INVARIANTS.find(id,along)  which combinations of the outputs never move — across the
                                   domain, or along one input (a clock: conserved quantities)
    HCC_INVARIANTS.symmetries(id)  scalings x → λ^k x that move nothing, applied before believed
    HCC_INVARIANTS.across(a,b)     laws across one bus link that neither laboratory states alone
    HCC_FEEDS                      the Sun, planets, named stars, galaxies, quasars — measured
                                   numbers, with provenance, fed into laboratory inputs
    HCC_STATS                      the classical statistics of the atlas's own catalogues

`describe(id)` returns a typed contract: inputs with units and domains, outputs,
the verifiers that guard it, and its prediction class — exact, numerical,
reference, conditional or exploratory. A laboratory never claims more than its
class allows.

## What is unusual here

**Refusals are first-class.** `bus.refusals` returns couplings the atlas declined
and the reason for each. A quantity bus that only reported what connects would be
half an instrument.

**Coincidences are tested for being coincidences.** Where two independently
computed numbers agree, the atlas varies a parameter neither side declares and
reports whether the agreement survives. Some do not, and it says so.

**Invariants are found, not declared.** Every laboratory is asked the same question —
which combinations of its outputs never move — by one finder that samples it through its
contract, keeps only minimal exact relations, names constants in closed form only to
1e-10, and applies every symmetry at random points before reporting it. The census is in
`api/invariants.json`: laws inside laboratories, and laws across the bus that no single
laboratory states (a Jeans mass carried into Hawking's law keeps M·T_H = ħc³/(8πG k_B)).

**Laws are found from the inputs.** The same census also asks what each output IS as a
function of the inputs that moved: a power law over every positive input at once, else the
smallest sum of at most three library terms plus a constant, for the output and — where that
is not exact — its square and reciprocal. It returns the f-sum rule π/2·ω_p², the multiplicity
2l + 1, a spinor's half angle cos(θ/2), σ_SB·T⁴ and M² = 1 + ZT from the laboratories
themselves (`laws` per laboratory in `api/invariants.json`).

**A field is drawn as its shape.** The Field Lab's default view is the geometry of the
field it integrates: level sets by marching tetrahedra (watertight, area and enclosed volume
measured), lines of −∇u from every source, a slice with isolines, |ψ|² coloured by the phase
of ψ, and for the 3D Ising lattice its exact domain walls — one dual plaquette per
antiparallel bond, whose area is the energy, E/N³ = −3 + 2W/N³. `HCC_FIELD.open(model,
preset)` and `HCC_FIELD.structure()` drive and read it.
Three laws are then read off the drawing: Gauss's law on every equipotential (Φ/Q → 1 once
`HCC_FIELD.converge()` has relaxed Poisson by SOR), the widest moment of a fixed isotherm of a
diffusing pulse (r² = ⟨r²⟩ exactly, whatever D, level or width), and the 3D Ising critical point
from crossing Binder cumulants with Wolff clusters (`HCC_FIELD.critical()`, T_c ≈ 4.51 J/k_B).

**A map of the Universe, at every level.** After Ménard & Shtarkman: the observer at the bottom,
the first light at the top, every object the atlas holds at its true distance — planets, 15 230
Hipparcos stars with a parallax, the Milky Way's nebulae, 4 341 galaxies, 5 959 quasars, and the
CMB at z = 1090 (13.86 Gpc comoving, radiation included). Linear, as in the original: everything
with a name sits in the bottom 2.4 %, quasars reach 55 %. Logarithmic: one strip, sixteen
decades, every level. The SDSS band the original fills is drawn as a labelled gap; the CMB band is
a Gaussian realisation, not the Planck map. `HCC_UMAP.open()`, `HCC_UMAP.stats()`.

**∃! The only possible laws.** `api/uniqueness.json` (from `scripts/uniqueness.mjs`): for each of
the 185 exact power laws, the smallest set of constants from {G, c, ħ, k_B, m_e, m_p} that makes it
consistent, and Buckingham's count of dimensionless groups. 48 are forced — the only formula units
allow — and 43 have their pure number named: π²/60 (Stefan–Boltzmann, forced by c, ħ, k_B), 2π/x_W
(Wien), π²/45 (radiation pressure), √(2π) (thermal wavelength), (3π²)^{2/3}/2 (Fermi),
2π/ζ(3/2)^{2/3} (BEC), π·e^−γ and e^γ/π² (BCS), π²/240 (Casimir), 3/5 (a uniform sphere),
π²/8 (the Local Group's timing mass), ln 2 (Landauer). 86 are free: their form is physics —
Bekenstein–Hawking's S = A/4 among them.

**∂ The law, one variable at a time.** Where no single closed form fits, `HCC_INVARIANTS.separable(id)`
holds every input but one, finds the law in that one (the smallest exact basis subset, parity (−1)^n
for integers, or an exact rational function P/Q), then the law of each coefficient in a second input.
The census records each one (`api/invariants.json`, `separable`, with its counts). From numbers alone it returns the Bethe–Weizsäcker formula with its pairing term, and the Lorentz
oscillator's absorption as a rational function of degrees (1, 4) with the laws of its coefficients.

**⟳ The Galaxy turns.** "What the catalogues say" fits the 15 544 embedded Hipparcos proper
motions within a kiloparsec with the Ogorodnikov–Milne field: (U, V, W)☉ = (10.4, 14.5, 7.5) km/s,
Oort A = 14.5 ± 0.8, B = −13.7 ± 0.6, C = −3.2, K = −3.7 km/s/kpc; Ω₀ = 28.1 ± 0.9 (Sgr A*'s proper
motion less the Sun's lead gives 29.3), a rotation curve flat within its error, κ/Ω₀ = 1.39.
Lindblad's relation joins two moments of one catalogue: −B/(A − B) = 0.486 ± 0.018 from the mean
flow's gradient, σ_V²/σ_U² = 0.496 ± 0.016 from the dispersion tensor of the residuals. The 3D
view draws every star's motion in three frames (seen from the Sun; reflex removed, beside the
measured shear field M·r; model removed). `HCC_STATS.oort()`, `HCC_STATS.flow(frame)`.

**🕸 The cosmic web.** The projected two-point function w_p(r_p) of the 4 341 galaxies against
randoms drawn through the same window (distances from the galaxies, directions from a smooth
mask), Landy–Szalay, summed along the line of sight so 20 % distance errors cannot touch it:
γ ≈ 2.0 over 0.5–10 Mpc, r₀ = 5.3 Mpc at γ = 1.8 (a lower bound; CfA: 1.77 and 5.4 h⁻¹ Mpc). The
minimal spanning tree is 26 % shorter than one through randoms and is drawn in 3D from the
supergalactic pole. `HCC_STATS.web()`, `HCC_STATS.skeleton(true)`.

**The laboratory audit.** Five laboratories were re-derived and re-measured point by point;
repaired: kdv refuses the steps where its integrator is unstable (dt·max c > 0.008), nuc says the
liquid drop puts the summit at Fe-58 where the measured masses put Ni-62, earth refuses its legacy
engine beyond ±1000 yr, localflow returns all seven declared outputs, spectrum takes its lowest
level and gap over j ≤ 2 whatever j_max is. `docs/verify-the-laboratory-audit.cjs`.

**The neighbourhood rides the Galaxy.** The disc now turns the right way (clockwise from the north
Galactic pole: the centre drifts toward l = 270° as the Sun moves toward Cygnus) and nothing near
the Sun flies in a straight line any more: every Hipparcos and named star follows Hill's equations
in the frame of the local standard of rest, with the Oort constant A this atlas measures from its
own proper motions and ν = √(4πGρ₀); nebulae, open clusters and arm tracers ride circular orbits
at their own radii and globular clusters stay at rest in the halo. The guiding centres move on
circles, so over gigayears the neighbourhood shears into arcs and phase-mixes into rings.
`docs/verify-the-stars-ride-the-galaxy.cjs`.

**Earth's axis keeps precessing.** The Vondrák series runs away outside its ±200 kyr window (the
pole fell onto the equator by ±1 Myr); past the window the axis continues on the precession cone,
one turn in 25 772 years with the obliquity on the 41-kyr cycle, joined to the fit with no jump.
`docs/verify-the-axis-keeps-precessing.cjs`.

**Topology, made visible.** The topology atlas opens on the Hopf fibration — 48 fibres on four
nested tori beside the base sphere, every one of the 1 128 pairs measured to link exactly once —
and on Gauss–Bonnet: a surface whose holes open one by one as a radius falls, χ counted as
V − E + F and the angle deficits summing to 2πχ exactly, the total curvature jumping only when a
hole opens. `docs/verify-topology-made-visible.cjs`.

**The laboratory bar.** One slim strip, always present above the time machine on every device
and never over the model: ⊞ with the number of laboratories (opens the full catalogue — search,
categories), ‹ the current laboratory › (tap for the catalogue, swipe or ‹ › or the [ ] keys to
walk), ⚙ its Controls, ◱ Multiview. Sheets rise from it like a mini-player's; on a phone lying on
its side it keeps to the left of the sheet column. A first visit is told once what it is.
`HCC_LAB_BAR.state()`, `.next()`, `.prev()`, `.catalogue()`, `.controls()`, `.multiview()`.

**☰ is a toolbox.** The left ☰ button (it did nothing on phones) opens one sheet of the tools
that act on the view — clean view, reset view, fullscreen, capture, day/night, share link, reset
motion, all laboratories — and the atlas-wide panels: navigator, objects, vectors, predictions,
invariants, the Trisphere, the Galaxy from above, Andromeda as we see it and from above.
`HCC_TOOLS.open()`, `.list()`.

**The Milky Way and Andromeda, alive.** Neither galaxy turns like a painted wheel any more.
Every star is carried by the shader at its own Ω(R) on a flat rotation curve; the arms are a
density wave turning at the pattern speed Ωp and TRAILING the rotation, lit by young stars only
where the wave is; the bar turns as one figure at Ωbar. Each disc also carries its diffuse light
— exponential disc, Sérsic bulge, the arms — with the dust lane on the side corotation puts it
(upstream inside, downstream outside), HII knots carried in the material frame for ~30 Myr each,
and M31's 10-kpc star-forming ring. M31 now leans the way the sky shows: its north-west half is
the near side (Hubble 1943) and its north-east half recedes (Rubin & Ford 1970), on the same
disc basis every catalogued galaxy uses. Seen from the Sun, the trails of nearby stars run from
where each star is now along its own ridden path. `HCC_MW.view()`, `.andromeda(faceOn)`,
`.state()`. `docs/verify-the-milky-way-is-alive.cjs`, `docs/verify-andromeda-is-alive.cjs`.

**The selection card never blankets what it describes.** On a phone a tap selects and opens a
PEEK on the laboratory bar — the name, one line, ◎ fly · ▴ open · ✕ close; open, the card rises
from the same place, under half the screen by default. It is rubber like every other sheet: drag
its grip to any height (remembered, never over the whole model), tap the grip to fold or open,
flick down to fold (from the peek, to let the object go), flick up to open full; on a desktop a
gold corner drags its width and height. The reader's choice is remembered for every later selection; a double tap
still flies to the object. `docs/verify-the-card-never-blankets.cjs`.

**Where the arms may live — the Galaxy's resonances, measured.** From the Oort constants this
atlas fits to 15 000 Hipparcos stars, Ω₀ = A − B = 28.1 ± 0.9 and κ₀ = √(−4B(A − B)) = 39.2 ± 1.3
km/s/kpc. Two resonance numbers follow, and both are findings: (Ω₀ − Ωp)/κ₀ = 0.003 ± 0.024 — the
Sun at the arms' corotation (Ωp = 28) — and (Ω₀ − Ωb)/κ₀ = −0.278 ± 0.026 ≈ −1/4 — the Sun 0.22 kpc
outside the bar's outer 4:1 resonance (Ωb = 39), the Hercules-stream resonance of Hunt & Bovy
(2018). The bar is fast (ℛ = 1.38); a four-armed wave at Ωp can live between 5.4 and 11.0 kpc,
which holds Sagittarius, the Local Spur and Perseus but not the outermost arm. The station
"Resonances" draws the frequency diagram (Ω, Ω ± κ/2, Ω ± κ/4) and the rings in the living Galaxy.
`HCC_STATS.resonances()`, `.showResonances()`. `docs/verify-where-the-arms-may-live.cjs`.

**Navier–Stokes on S³, integrated (laboratory `nsflow`).** The atlas's S³ programme names one
exact non-stationary solution, u = K + a e^{−νκt}(Φ_t^Y)_* v₀ (a rigid Killing rotation plus a
curl shell carried by the flow of Y = (1 − 2/μ)K₊ + (1 + 2/μ)K₋ while it decays). This laboratory
substitutes it into the equation: the curl of the residual ∂ₜu + ∇ᵤu + νAu is ≈ 1e-8 of the
convective term's (zero ⇔ a pressure gradient, since H¹(S³) = 0), and of order one if the shell is
carried the wrong way. Thousands of tracers are then carried by it on S³; div u = 0 keeps them
uniform, so their mean |u|² measures the energy on the exact law. An honest ledger sits beside it:
PROVEN (exact families, measured), CONDITIONAL (the relative singular branch, assumptions S₀…S₄),
OPEN (the Clay Millennium problem: a finite-time blow-up WITH a smooth,
compactly supported force was announced on 8 September 2026 — OpenAI, Lean-certified by its own
account; Alpöge and Buckmaster hours earlier — and is not accepted by the Clay Institute; WITHOUT a
force it is open; nothing here claims either). And the Millennium
problem that IS solved — Poincaré, by Ricci flow — is about this very sphere: the round S³ shrinks
to a point at t = R²/4. `docs/verify-navier-stokes-on-s3-integrated.cjs`.

**The Controls filter folds into one key.** The filter strip no longer sits over the Controls
sheet: it lives behind ⌕ in the sheet's header rail (which shows how many settings you have
changed), opens on a tap or on "/", and closing it clears the filter. A short sheet shows its
controls directly under the rail, and a zoomed sheet no longer sinks under the time machine.
`docs/verify-the-filter-folds-into-one-key.cjs`.

**The atlas knows its own shape — meaning goes round, number goes one way.** The relation graph
(371 distinct relations) is connected, and its first Betti number b₁ = E − V + 1
= 251 counts the independent cycles in which every laboratory is explained by others that are
explained, in the end, by it. The quantity bus (57 links) has no cycle at
all — by rule: a bus with a cycle would be an oscillator, not a machine. The first mode of the
relation Laplacian (λ₂ = 0.634), with no label consulted, cuts the atlas into two halves — the
observed sky and the sphere — joined by a seam of relations, and the cut obeys Cheeger's
inequality; the live counts are in `HCC_ATLAS_SELF.shape()`. On the Trisphere, "◐ the two halves of the atlas" colours them and draws the seam.
`HCC_ATLAS_SELF.shape()`. `docs/verify-the-atlas-knows-its-own-shape.cjs`.

**The black holes at the centres, traced.** Sgr A* and M31* are no longer a ball and a torus: their
gateways are ray-traced in the fragment shader — every pixel a Schwarzschild null geodesic — so the
shadow, the photon ring at √27 GM/c², the lensed far side of the disk and its Doppler-beamed
approaching limb emerge. Escaping rays carry no invented stars; the real sky shows through. The
disk turns phase-locked to the ISCO period. Sgr A* is drawn 20° from face-on, clockwise on the sky
(GRAVITY 2018; EHT 2022 disfavours i > 50°); M31* in its host's plane (declared). The size is a
prediction the atlas passes: 2√27·GM/(c²D) from its own numbers gives 52.0 μas for Sgr A* (EHT
ring 51.8 ± 2.3) and 39.7 μas for M87* (42 ± 3). A sign error in the relativistic laboratory's
Doppler factor — which dimmed the approaching limb — is fixed. `HCC_BH.view('sgra'|'m31')`,
`HCC_BH.shadow()`. `docs/verify-the-black-holes-are-traced.cjs`.

**Deep time — what the clock can reach, and what happens there.** The clock runs to ±2.5×10¹³ years.
On it the universe cools by flat ΛCDM with this atlas's H₀ and Ω_m (carried in logarithms); a black
hole absorbs the CMB until the universe is colder than its Hawking temperature — for Sgr A* that is
~562 billion years from now — and only then evaporates, over ~1.5×10⁸⁷ years, 74 decades beyond the
clock's edge (said, not faked); M31 falls along the Kahn–Woltjer cycloid the atlas solves from its own
numbers, first passage 3.28 Gyr on the radial solution (the transverse motion puts it near 4.5 Gyr);
and in the black-hole laboratory "⏳ on the atlas clock" lets a primordial hole born at the Big Bang
evaporate on the atlas's own time — the one dying now was born with 1.73×10¹¹ kg.
`docs/verify-deep-time.cjs`.

**Spacetime, 2+1, boosted live.** The relativity laboratory's light cone is light running along its
generators at c, and 1 331 events are carried through the Lorentz boost in the vertex shader, sliding
along the hyperboloids of constant proper time and distance; each keeps its causal colour, the sign of
s², at every β. The lab's clocks tick every γ of the ship's time, its plane of simultaneity tilts, and a
flash stays a circle of radius ct in every frame. `docs/verify-spacetime-boosted-live.cjs`.

**The last merger of the Local Group (laboratory `bbh`).** Sgr A* and M31* spiral together in the
gravitational-wave regime: the Peters inspiral and the quadrupole waveform, Φ = −(2/η)(ητ/5M)^{5/8},
evaluated at every point of the orbital plane at its retarded time, so the two-armed spiral of h₊ is
drawn as it is; then the end state from numerical-relativity fits for non-spinning holes and the
l = m = 2 ringdown. From the atlas's own masses: η = 0.02796, 0.200 % of 1.44×10⁸ M☉ radiated
(5.2×10⁵² J), remnant spin 0.094, recoil 8.6 km/s, ringdown at 86 μHz damping in 2.25 h — just below
LISA's band — and 40 Myr in the pulsar-timing band before the end. What is not computed (the galaxies'
merger, dynamical friction, the final parsec) is said to be. `docs/verify-the-last-merger.cjs`.

**The merger on the atlas clock.** The two holes also merge in the atlas itself, every phase a pure
function of the epoch — the same state at one day per second and at a billion years per second. M31
falls along the timing cycloid until it crosses 1 kpc (+3.284 Gyr, with no jump); the Milky Way's
nucleus (Sgr A* in its 2.5×10⁷ M☉ nuclear star cluster) then sinks by Chandrasekhar dynamical friction,
t_df = (1.17/ln Λ) r₀²v_c/(GM) = 367 Myr (r₀ = 1 kpc and v_c = 250 km/s declared; the merged galaxy is
not modelled and M31's disc fades into it); the final parsec is assumed crossed; at +3.652 Gyr the
remnant — 1.44×10⁸ M☉, spin 0.094 — replaces the pair, and a gravitational-wave front leaves the centre
at exactly c, passing the Sun ~26 700 years later with h ≈ 1.6×10⁻¹¹ — the Earth–Sun distance breathing
by about a metre. The toolbox's "Watch the holes merge on the atlas clock" sets it running.
`HCC_BH.timeline()`, `HCC_BH.watchMerger()`. `docs/verify-the-merger-on-the-clock.cjs`.

**One clock for the laboratories, and the phase portrait of any of them.** "⏱ couple lab time to the
time machine" (in the laboratory panel) makes every routed laboratory run on k·dt, where k is the time
machine's rate over the rate at coupling — speed the machine up and every cyclic laboratory turns
faster, pause it and they stop (k ≤ 10⁶; negative rates are not passed on; integrators keep their own
step bounds). At large k each frame is a stroboscopic sample, and "◌ phase portrait" draws it: the two
most varying moving parts of the scene, any two bus quantities, or one quantity against itself a few
frames earlier (Takens delay embedding), with its correlation dimension (Grassberger–Procaccia) —
≈ 1 for a limit cycle, ≈ 2 for a torus. `docs/verify-one-clock-for-the-laboratories.cjs`.

**The fluid's modes are spins.** S³ is the group SU(2), its isometries are SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R, and every
field on it splits into spins (j_L, j_R). The Navier–Stokes curl shells E_{k,σ} are (k/2+1, k/2) and
(k/2, k/2+1): dimension (k+1)(k+3), curl eigenvalue μ = C_L − C_R = σ(k+2), Stokes eigenvalue
κ = 2(C_L + C_R) − 4 = k(k+4); the scalar harmonics of the trisphere and the modes laboratory are (n/2, n/2);
the Killing fields are (1,0) ⊕ (0,1), the two Lie algebras. This is MEASURED, not assumed: both SU(2)
factors act on the shells the laboratory builds numerically, and the traces of the actions equal
χ_{j_L}(θ)(2j_R+1) and χ_{j_R}(θ)(2j_L+1) to 1e-14. The Weitzenböck law A = curl² − 4 becomes Casimir
arithmetic, (C_L − C_R)² − 2(C_L + C_R) = (d² − 1)(s² − 1) with d = j_L − j_R, s = j_L + j_R + 1, so
curl² = 2(C_L + C_R) exactly when the spins differ by one. And the flow itself now runs on the
trisphere: "〰 the Navier–Stokes flow on the trisphere" carries tracers by the exact solution, coloured
by shell against rigid rotation. `docs/verify-the-fluid-modes-are-spins.cjs`. And the two relations this
added (nsflow–su2, nsflow–eig) moved exactly one laboratory across the atlas's own Fiedler cut: the cosmic
microwave background, whose Fiedler coordinate became the nearest to zero of all laboratories. One relation
later (cosmicweb–nsflow) the spherical harmonics took that place and the CMB the fifth: the robust fact is
that the seam between the observed sky and the sphere runs through the harmonic analysis of a sphere — the
CMB and the spherical harmonics both stand on it. The halves are oriented by the main sequence and the
laboratories on the seam are named, live. `docs/verify-the-atlas-knows-its-own-shape.cjs`.

**The web has relief.** Every supercluster, wall, cluster and void of the atlas is now drawn as a
constrained realization of the ΛCDM density field rather than a wireframe: P(k) from the Eisenstein–Hu
transfer function with the atlas's H₀ and Ω_m and Planck 2018 nₛ = 0.9649, σ₈ = 0.8111; the Zel'dovich map
x = q + D·s truncated at the non-linear scale; Hoffman–Ribak constraints making each structure a peak, a
sheet of peaks or a trough; galaxies sampled as a lognormal tracer (b = 1.8), coloured void / sheet /
filament / node by the deformation tensor (T-web) and brightened by the Zel'dovich density. Built in a Web
Worker, nearest first. The growth is read off the atlas clock AT THE TIME EACH STRUCTURE'S LIGHT LEFT: the
Hercules–Corona Borealis wall at z ≈ 1.8 shows D = 0.45; run the clock back and the web dissolves into the
near-uniform early universe; run it forward and it freezes, because Λ stops growth at
D∞/D₀ = (5/6)Ω_m^{1/3}Ω_Λ^{−1/3}B(5/6, 2/3)/g₀ = 1.3968 — the web can only ever grow 40% more than today.
And it is Navier–Stokes: the Zel'dovich map is the inviscid limit of Burgers' equation (pressureless
Navier–Stokes for a potential flow), solved exactly by Hopf–Cole; the cosmic-web laboratory plots both —
one curve before shell crossing, and after it a shock that holds exactly the matter the three Zel'dovich
streams share. A realization, not a reconstruction. `HCC_WEB_RELIEF.state()`.
`docs/verify-the-web-has-relief.cjs`.

**The CMB sky, as physics paints it.** The last-scattering wall of the Observable world is no longer a
procedural mottling: it is one full-sky realization of THIS atlas's cosmology. CAMB (the Boltzmann code),
run for H₀ = 68.43, Ω_m = 0.305, ω_b = 0.02237, nₛ = 0.9649, τ = 0.0544, σ₈ = 0.8111, gives the lensed
TT/EE/TE/BB spectra to ℓ = 2000; healpy draws correlated T, Q, U at Nside 1024 with a 5′ beam and measures
them back (σ_T 109.27 μK vs 109.33 from the spectrum; band power 0.9997). Three ways to see it: the
Planck collaboration's own parchment colour table over ±300 μK; the colour it WAS — at last scattering
the sky glowed at T₀(1+z*) = 2973 K, a halogen-lamp white computed from Planck's law through the CIE 1931
observer, with the 10⁻⁵ anisotropy invisible unless a slider multiplies it; and the polarization drapery,
line-integral convolution on the GPU, flowing. The CMB laboratory shows the spectra: peaks at
ℓ = 220, 534, 811, 1123, 1417, 1721 = ℓ_A(n − φ_n) with ℓ_A = π/θ* = 300.87, and every EE crest in a TT
trough — velocity out of phase with density. CAMB's age of the universe (13.7072 Gyr) agrees with the
atlas's own integral (13.7079) to 0.001 Gyr. A realization with the exact spectrum, not the measured
Planck map. `HCC_CMB_SKY.state()`. `scripts/build-cmb-sky.py`, `data/CMB-SKY-SOURCES.md`,
`docs/verify-the-cmb-sky.cjs`.

**The real local web — found, not listed.** 17 300 galaxies with measured redshifts (the Stellarium 23.4
catalogue, redshifts from NED/HyperLEDA) are placed at their comoving distances in redshift space, and the
density contrast is taken the robust way for a compilation: a band-pass δ = n₈/n₄₀, masked by the zone of
avoidance and by shot noise (reach 179 Mpc). With no name consulted, out come the Local Supercluster,
Perseus–Pisces (8° and 4% from where the atlas had placed it by hand), Coma, Pavo–Indus (14°) and two
unnamed superclusters, and 14 voids found as maximal empty spheres — each confirmed twice, in the smoothed
contrast and in the raw galaxy counts against the same shell in the same direction. Every rich cluster the
mask does not hide stands overdense; Norma, behind the Milky Way, is masked. Drawn as a ray-marched volume
with every galaxy a point; the found structures are selectable. Contrast above ~40 Mpc is suppressed by
construction. The CMB wall now dims while you look at the local universe and brightens as you stand back.
`HCC_LOCAL_WEB.meta()`, `scripts/build-local-web.py`, `data/LOCAL-WEB-SOURCES.md`,
`docs/verify-the-real-local-web.cjs`.

**Back is always there.** After any transition — a world tab, the laboratory bar, the trail, a jump from a card —
the first element of the trail is ← Back, on every screen and on the phone. The two back-stacks (the
camera-exact one and the route history) are stamped from one counter, so Back always undoes the latest step,
follows the route so the trail and the scene agree, and restores the camera the jump saved. With nowhere to go
it stays visible, dimmed. `HCC_NAV.back()`. `docs/verify-back-is-always-there.cjs`.

**The Local Group's future, by law — and it is probably not a merger.** The atlas's first account of the
Milky Way–Andromeda encounter was Kahn & Woltjer's radial cycloid: a collision 3.3 Gyr from now. A new
laboratory (lgmerge) integrates it instead: two galaxies (Hernquist haloes, Miyamoto–Nagai discs, bulges),
pulled by each other and slowed by Chandrasekhar dynamical friction, whose one free number (lnΛ = 0.55) is
calibrated ONCE to the N-body merger of van der Marel et al. (2012) — first passage 4.0 Gyr, coalescence
5.8 Gyr against their 5.86. Applied to today's data, the tangential velocity of 57 ± 35 km/s measured by
Gaia and HST (van der Marel et al. 2019): a first passage at 4.5 Gyr at ~126 kpc and NO merger within
14 Gyr. Sampled over the errors: P(merger ≤ 5 Gyr) ≈ 6%, ≤ 10 Gyr ≈ 25%, ≤ 14 Gyr ≈ 33% — without M33
and the LMC, which Sawala et al. (2025) show also matter, and that is declared. The stars are test
particles (Toomre & Toomre 1972), 1 500 per disc in a Web Worker: in the calibration scenario they throw tidal
tails at the first passage and settle into a spheroidal remnant; the black holes ride the centres, sink only
when the cores coalesce, and merge with the numerical-relativity recoil. Energy is conserved to 1.6e-8
without friction; the discs sit in equilibrium before the encounter. `HCC_API` instrument `lgmerge`.
`docs/verify-the-local-group-future.cjs`.

**The Discovery Explorer — the ledger of what the atlas has learned.** Findings lived only in prose; now they
are a ledger (`HCC_DISCOVERIES`) and a place (laboratory `discover`): a constellation per domain, a star per
claim shaped by its kind — ★ found here, ✓ confirms the literature from first principles, ⚡ the atlas
correcting itself, ≈ a coincidence tested — with arcs where two share a laboratory, the atlas's corrections of
itself drawn in red (the probable flyby supersedes the textbook collision), and the open LEADS, each with its
next concrete step, left for whoever continues (M33 and the LMC in the Local Group future, the measured Planck
sky, a homogeneous survey for the local web, Spin(4) selection rules for the Navier–Stokes nonlinearity, …).
▶ flies through them all; every laboratory's passport shows the discoveries that live in it. Every entry names
a verifier that exists and runs on every build. `HCC_DISCOVERIES.list()`, `.leads()`, `.byLab(id)`.
`docs/verify-the-discovery-ledger.cjs`.

**The colour of cosmic time — and one universe, drawn once.** Distance is time: every place is seen when its light
left, so one colour now says both, the same everywhere in the atlas. A slice through the observable ball, always
facing the camera, shows every radius in the colour of the epoch it shows — the gold present, the cyan-white
cosmic noon, the blue of reionization, the violet first light, the dark ages reddening outward, and at the rim the
2973 K glow of last scattering — with the giant structures standing in front of and behind it in the same colours,
and a legend of all cosmic time on one logarithmic bar with the clock's position. Before the first stars the colour
IS the relic radiation at T₀(1+z) (Planck's law through the CIE observer); after them the hue marks the epoch (a
declared scale) and the brightness is the measured star-formation rate (Madau & Dickinson 2014, peak z = 1.86); the
clock moves it (t_emit + Δt). The distance–epoch chain includes radiation and lands where CAMB does: last scattering
at χ = 45.121 Gly against 45.133 (0.03%), age 13.7069 Gyr against 13.7072, recombination at 371 kyr. The giant
structures in the solar chain are the continuation of the solar model and are left exactly as they are (AU, the Sun
at the origin, ecliptic J2000); Horizons reads the same catalogue by the same formula (raDecDir × D_C) with its own
instruments. Carrying the Horizons group bodily into the solar chain was tried and undone: its shaders measure
distance in Gly and washed out the solar sky at 1 Gly → GLY_AU AU. What is carried in is only what has no scale
inside it — the spheres of cosmic time — in a holder at exactly that scale, so the nesting runs unbroken from the
planets to last scattering, sphere in sphere about one Sun. The tabs say what they are: ☀ Sun → Cosmos, ◯ Horizons.
`HCC_COSMIC_TIME`. `docs/verify-the-colour-of-cosmic-time.cjs`.

**Space forms S³/Γ — their spectra, and whether the sky could show them (laboratory `s3gamma`).** If the universe is
a three-sphere it may be one only up to identification. From the Spin(4) dictionary, a character sum over Γ's
conjugacy classes gives every Laplace multiplicity exactly: the Poincaré dodecahedral space S³/I* keeps only
k = 0, 12, 20, 24, 30, 32, 36, 40, … (the Molien series of I*), the octahedral starts at 8, the tetrahedral at 6, and
Σm_k/Σ(k+1)² → 1/|Γ| (Weyl). The images of the observer are drawn — for I* the 120 vertices of the 600-cell, each with
12 neighbours at 36° — with the last-scattering sphere around each. Matched circles (Cornish, Spergel & Starkman)
need θ_min R < 2χ_LSS: R < 144 Gly for the Poincaré space, 115 octahedral, 86 tetrahedral — all below this atlas's
entire 95% curvature band (414–4540 Gly), while lens spaces of order p ≳ 29 could still show circles (L(60,1): 48%).
A circle search on the real sky would therefore test the atlas's curvature branch. `docs/verify-the-space-forms.cjs`.

**Circles in the sky — the search, with its null.** The laboratory runs the matched-circle statistic
S(ψ) = 2ΣT₁T₂/Σ(T₁² + T₂²) over back-to-back pairs (the pairs a homogeneous S³/Γ makes, turned by θ_min — 36° for
I*), every twist and both orientations by two FFTs, coarse (≈ 2.8°, 12 000 directions) to fine (≈ 1.4°, then 0.35°).
The circle about −c is the antipode of the circle about c run backwards, n′(φ) = −n(−φ), so every even multipole
"matches" itself — unfiltered, a pure quadrupole sky scores S = 1 — and the modes along the circle longer than 15°
are dropped. On random skies the null is S ≈ 0.60–0.73 with σ = 0.025; pairs injected with the Poincaré twist are
recovered at their own radius, within 0.5° of their centre and at ψ = 38° for 36°, 10–13σ above it. In the page it
runs on the atlas's CAMB sky and recovers about 4 injected pairs in 5 there (the CMB decorrelates within a degree).
The measured Planck sky is not searched: it is not reachable from this build. `docs/verify-the-circles-in-the-sky.cjs`.

**Seeing the sky through its mask — the Wiener filter and the MASTER spectrum (CMB laboratory).** An exact
spherical-harmonic transform on L+1 Gauss–Legendre rings (round trip to 10⁻¹³). The Wiener filter — the most probable
sky given masked, noisy data, (S⁻¹ + YᵀN⁻¹Y) a = YᵀN⁻¹d — is solved by preconditioned conjugate gradients in harmonic
space: on the full sky it is exactly C/(C+N)·a_obs (10⁻¹⁵, one iteration); masked, its error is uncorrelated with it
(ρ = 0.001 over 24 skies, the orthogonality principle of a posterior mean; the naive cut-sky estimate's is ρ = −0.71),
and it paints the holes with the large scales (correlation ≈ 0.5 inside a 35% cut). MASTER inverts the coupling the
mask puts between multipoles, M_ℓℓ′ = (2ℓ′+1)/4π Σ(2ℓ″+1) W_ℓ″ (ℓ ℓ′ ℓ″; 0 0 0)²: columns built by pushing unit
harmonics through the apodised, band-limited mask equal the 3j formula to 3×10⁻¹⁵, and over 300 masked skies MASTER
is unbiased (χ²/dof 1.14) while dividing by f_sky is not (21.4; ℓ = 2, 3 read 24% low). The sky is drawn from this
atlas's CAMB spectrum; Planck data are not reachable from this build. Not done: the pure pseudo-Cℓ for B-modes (spin-2).
`HCC_CMB_WF.run({L, bDeg, lN, seed, R})`. `docs/verify-the-wiener-filter.cjs`.

**The fluid of the three-sphere — Navier–Stokes beyond the exact solutions (laboratory `nsgal`).** The exact
solutions live on one curl shell and never exchange energy; a real fluid does. Here Navier–Stokes on the unit S³ is
solved in the Spin(4) curl shells k = 0 … 3, both helicities ((k+1)(k+3) modes each, curl e = μe, μ = ±(k+2), 100
modes): da/dt = −νκa + ⟨e, u × ω⟩, κ = k(k+4), the Lamb vector through an exact quadrature in Hopf coordinates. The
truncation keeps what the equation keeps — energy and helicity without viscosity (10⁻¹¹), the six Killing components
(the angular momenta of so(4) = su(2) ⊕ su(2)) always, to rounding — so the fluid forgets everything but six numbers
and ends in the rigid rotation they fix at t = 0 (E∞ = ½|P_K a₀|², H∞ = 2(|P₊a₀|² − |P₋a₀|²), Ω∞ = 8E∞), reached to
six digits. Started on the atlas's exact solution it follows it to 7×10⁻¹⁰: two independent routes to one flow. The
shells talk only as Spin(4) allows — the Lamb vector of two shells lands in exactly the Clebsch–Gordan shells (120 of
120), never in the rigid rotation, and a Beltrami shell does not talk to itself. Drawn in the trisphere's own
four-dimensional turn: streamlines with beads, tracers coloured by the sign of the helicity density, and beside it the
phase space (E, H, Ω) with the realizability cone |H| ≤ √(2EΩ), the Beltrami ray of every shell and the star where the
fluid must end. Open: without viscosity the 52-mode fluid thermalises towards Kraichnan's absolute equilibrium (19% off at
t = 300, 2–7% at 2000, 0.1–3.5% at 6000) — exactly, or is there an unnamed invariant? `docs/verify-the-fluid-of-the-three-sphere.cjs`.

**The hunt for a hidden law — does the fluid of S³ conserve something nobody named? (v4.339, in `nsgal`).** Asked of
the equations, not guessed: a polynomial Q is conserved by the truncated Euler flow iff ∇Q · f(a) = 0 for every state,
which is linear in Q's coefficients, so the conserved polynomials of degree d are the null space of a Gram matrix of
random-state rows, counted by eigenvalues that fall off a cliff (to 10⁻¹⁶) exactly at them (`nsgInvariantHunt(B, d)`,
own Householder + QL eigen-solver `nsgEigSym`, run in a worker, the spectrum drawn as "the cliff"). The theory names
six angular momenta L (the Killing modes), E and H of the rest, and their products. Found: exactly 6 linear and 23
quadratic invariants at K = 1 and K = 2 (22 and 52 modes; 253 and 1378 unknowns) and exactly 68 cubic ones at K = 1
(2024 unknowns: 56 products of L, 6 L·E, 6 L·H), every named one in the null space to 10⁻¹⁶, cliffs of 10¹²–10¹⁴.
No hidden law at these degrees: the slow approach to Kraichnan's equilibrium is relaxation. The census is tested on
a system whose laws are known — the free rigid body (0 linear, 2 quadratic) and the symmetric top, whose unnamed L₃ it
reports as hidden = 1. Replay: track `noHiddenLaw` (op `fluid.invariants`). Corrected on the way: the K = 2 truncation
has 52 modes (3 + 8 + 15 per helicity), not 56. `docs/verify-the-hunt-for-a-hidden-law.cjs`.

**The anatomy of a forced blow-up — the 2026 exponents and the window every theorem leaves (laboratory `nsblow`,
v4.340).** The forced Navier–Stokes blow-up announced by OpenAI on 8 September 2026 (Lean-certified by its own
account; not accepted by the Clay Institute) is an axisymmetric swirl core in anisotropic similarity variables:
τ = 1 − t, X = r²/2q, η = z/q^D, u_θ = q^{−A}√(2X)F, u_z = q^{−A}U, r·u_r = X·v₀, A = ½ + h, D = ½ − h, 0 < h < 1/100
(as quoted in arXiv 2609.17642; the profile construction retold in arXiv 2609.35406). The profile is theirs; the
exponents are public, and from them alone (`fbExponents`, `fbCriteria`, `fbWindow`): Beale–Kato–Majda and
Prodi–Serrin hold for h ≥ 0; Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák (‖u‖_{L³} ∝ τ^{−4h/3}), no Type I and no Leray
self-similarity demand h > 0 (all three fail at h = 0); Leray's energy (E ∝ τ^{½−3h}, finite dissipation) demands
h < 1/6 — one window 0 < h < 1/6, the construction 16× inside. One exponent pays for everything: Γ = r·u_θ, the core
Reynolds number, z/r and √τ‖u‖∞ all ∝ τ^{−h}; without a force max r·u_θ cannot grow, so h is the rate the force must
feed the swirl (in the core frame the swirl spins up as e^{hs}). In (ln Γ, ln E, ln‖u‖∞) every h is a ray, all rays lie
in one plane with normal (−4, 1, 1): E‖u‖∞/Γ⁴ is the same for every h and τ (1.7276467 on the lab's core, leading
order). The core drawn is an ILLUSTRATIVE Burgers–Oseen profile in those variables (divergence-free, measured
exponents). Beside it, the empirical ladder of unstable singularities (arXiv 2509.14185): λₙ ≈ 1 + 1/(1.4187n +
1.0863) for Boussinesq/Euler, λₙ ≈ 1/(1.1459n + 0.9723) for IPM. Tracks `blowupWindow`, `blowupInvariant` (op
`blowup.window`); lead `blowup-profile`. `docs/verify-the-anatomy-of-a-forced-blow-up.cjs`.

**The Cycles world, in order — and its sections (v4.340).** The fourteen frames are one strict, numbered hierarchy
(`HCC_CYCLE_GROUPS`): 0 · the whole (all cycles, all models on one stage); I · what repeats (seasons, precession,
galactic year, reference planes); II · when clocks meet (phase space, resonances · Saros, linked analysis); III · what
people built and drew (Antikythera, ancient chronometry, wheels of time); IV · what happened once (the galactic
butterfly). The view <select> is generated from the same table (it was a second hand-typed list with other names and
two frames missing); every frame says what it is; the multiphase/chronometry observatory folds away where it is not
the subject; the dashboard is grouped in families (Moon & eclipses · Earth · Sun · beyond), each period tagged by how
the atlas knows it (measured / derived / defined / predicted / approximate / model). One set of constants (the month
and year are `CYC_*`, the Metonic cycle is 19 tropical years by construction, 0.087 d short of 235 months; the
Antikythera constants no longer re-typed) and one phase (`cycLinkedPhaseOf` reads `cyclePhase`, with each cycle's
zero). The Antikythera hands are anchored to the sky by the Moon's mean elements (`cycMeanElements`, Meeus ch. 47)
and its Saros pointer glows inside the eclipse window (`cycEclipseWindow`): 17 of 17 catalogued eclipses, 30 of 150
new moons. The phase torus has a Poincaré section (`cycStrobe`): B read each time A comes round, a rotation by
ρ = P_A/P_B mod 1 that obeys the three-distance theorem — 1068 sections on 267 pairs, never more than three gap
lengths, the longest the sum of the other two; 19/235 among the convergents of month/year. The Saros is found in a
section (`cycSarosSection`): at every new moon the (node F, apsis M′) point returns nearest its start at lunation 223
(then 446, 669), and the Inex 358 lands on the opposite node. Ledger `sarosInSection`, `threeGaps`,
`antikytheraAnchored` (new domain "Cycles & time"); op `cycles.section`. `docs/verify-the-cycles-in-order.cjs`.

**The Stroboscope — resonances across space, time and parameters (laboratory `strobe`, v4.341).** A stroboscope
looks at a motion only at the flashes of its own clock, and whatever the motion shares with that clock stands still.
SPACE: the atlas's exact Navier–Stokes solution on S³ carries its curl shell k along Y = (1 − 2/μ)K₊ + (1 + 2/μ)K₋,
which as a rotation of ℝ⁴ is two rotations with frequencies 2 and 4/(k+2) (`carrierMatrix`, `carrierKnot`). The ratio is
rational for every shell, so every carrier orbit closes: torus knots T(k+2, 2) for odd k — the trefoil at k = 1, the
cinquefoil at k = 3 — and unknotted circles for even k, the windings counted on the real flow α q β
(`carrierWinding`, closing to 1e-15); and the solution is periodic in time, u(t + π(k+2)/gcd(k,4)) = u(t) to 2e-15,
both helicities, never earlier (`carrierReturn`). Drawn on three Clifford tori in the carrier's invariant planes, with
tracers flashed every T_s: at the pattern period they freeze, at p/q of it they form rosettes. TIME: the atlas's clocks
read at a flash period T, S(T) = Σ exp(−½(d/σ)²) the soft count of clocks returning together (`strobeScore`,
`strobePeaks`, named by `strobeName`), against a null of periods jittered ±5% (`strobeNull`); locked to the new moon
(`strobeLocked`) the Moon's best return within 1000 lunations is the Saros, 223 — and 300 jittered Moons match it with
p ≈ 0.16: the Saros is real and not improbable. PARAMETERS: Thomae's popcorn of closing ratios ρ, with the exact
carriers at ρ = 2/(k+2). Ledger `carrierKnots` (found), `sarosChance` (tested); ops `strobe.carrier`, `strobe.saros`;
lead `strobe-fluid` (the K = 1 truncation is only a rigid rotation — k = 1 shells cannot talk to each other).
`docs/verify-the-stroboscope.cjs`.

**The Formula Portal and the corpus audit (laboratories `formulas` and `vstretch`, v4.342).** The ten manuscripts of the
S³ Navier–Stokes programme display 5201 formulas (data/formula-atlas.json, schema `hcc.formula-atlas/1`), 1801 of them
distinct by normalised hash; 674 are carried by more than one manuscript. The portal lays them out as a sky — each
manuscript a constellation, each section an arm, bridges between constellations weighted by the formulas they share —
searchable (`formulaSearch`), typeset on demand (KaTeX fetched lazily; the LaTeX as written without it), linked by
section to the laboratory that computes it (`FORMULA_LAB_LINKS`), and checked on the spot where the atlas can
(`FORMULA_CHECKS`, 17 checks, op `formula.check`). Thirteen hold: the curl spectrum, the carrier weights c_τ(k,σ),
Casimir rigidity Δ = k(k+4)/(k+2), the random-Grassmannian variance law (Monte Carlo within 1%), Q(E₁,E₁) ⊂ E₂, the
Korn ladder 2‖Def u‖²/‖u‖² = k(k+4), the Hopf-filament pairing gap 2√min(c, 1−c), the Weyl–zeta residue 2/3, the
curvature of the shell connection ‖Ω‖ = 4k/(k+2), the rotor identity curl Q(u,v) = ½(μ_v − μ_u)[u,v], and — new — the
Vandermonde law of vortex stretching: ∫Def u(ω,ω) = −Σ_{a < b < c}(μ_a−μ_b)(μ_a−μ_c)(μ_b−μ_c)∫u_a·(u_b×u_c) for any sum
of curl levels (1e-10; one or two levels cannot stretch; the triple product of three shells vanishes unless
k_a + k_b + k_c is even, so the smallest stretching triad is E₁₊ + E₁₋ + E₂; laboratory `vstretch`, `vdmLaw`). Four fail
as stated: the boxed rational counting law of Λ_h below its Frobenius threshold (F00007); route P₁ of the terminal
lock — the stretching of a 𝒥-symmetric field is 𝒥-EVEN, not odd (S(𝒥x) = S(x) to 1e-9; `s3tcStretchParityField`; the
s3lock laboratory, which had the same sign, is revised); the shell commutator bound ‖[u_α,u_β]‖ ≤ C(k_αk_β)^{1/2} (the
commutator is ∝ k + 2 for a Killing probe, so the capacity threshold s > 9 + 4τ₀ is the convergence of the manuscript's
series, not an established class); and inf Γ_N > 0 (exact resonances κ₄ + κ₅ = κ₇ couple 27–57% of the energy into E₇).
Ledger `vandermondeStretch` (found), `stretchParityRevised` (revises), `corpusAudit` (tested); lead `corpus-open`.
`docs/verify-the-formula-portal.cjs`, `docs/verify-vortex-stretching-is-vandermonde.cjs`.

**The display is a stroboscope — and the S³ spectral ladder beside the φ-ladder (v4.343).** Every animated view is
sampled at the presented frame rate; a hand that turns more than half a turn between frames is seen turning backwards
(the wagon-wheel alias). The atlas measures its presented rate every frame (`HCC_DISPLAY`, `hccDisplaySample`: the median
of the last ninety intervals, robust to stalls — 60 Hz on a desktop, ~1.7 Hz in a software renderer); cyclic hands ask
`hccAliasGuard` how many turns they make per presented frame, measured from the epochs the frames actually showed —
true below ¼, flagged to ½, faded past ½ (Nyquist) instead of lying — on the Antikythera's Sun, Moon, anomaly, node and
phase hands and the three Saros hands. The Stroboscope places flashes at exact flow times (so its rosettes are true at
any frame rate) and reports the display rate, flashes per frame and tracer turn per frame (`strobeFrameBudget`).
In the FBS3R world a second coordinate on the same scale axis: the φ-ladder counts a length geometrically,
N = log_φ(ℓ/l_P); the cosmic S³ counts it arithmetically as the curl shell k with wavelength 2πR/(k+2)
(`s3LadderK`, `s3LadderN`, `s3LadderKofN`) — switch φ / S³ / both. The S³ tower (k = 0 … 48) carries measured exact
structure: the Killing drift ladder (2Q(X₃,·) on E_{k,σ} has spectrum ±c_τ·2m, m = −j_τ … j_τ, (2j_{−τ}+1)-fold; the full
spectrum of −D² to 5e-14; `s3DriftLadder`, check F00967), the homogeneous addition theorem (Σ e_i e_iᵀ = (k+1)(k+3)/(3V)·P_x,
1e-14; check F01072), the 26 exact triad resonances κ_a + κ_b = κ_c with allowed even-parity triangles up to k = 48
(`s3ExactTriads`), and the absolute-helicity drain 2νκ|μ|. A coordinate, not a claim that the two ladders are one physics.
Ledger `twoLadders` (confirms), `displayStroboscope` (tested). `docs/verify-the-display-is-a-stroboscope.cjs`.

**The Oracle — one question across every kind of knowledge (v4.344).** The atlas knows things in eight places: its
laboratories, its ledger of discoveries, its open leads, the relations between laboratories, the checks that run here,
the 1801 formulas of the S³ programme, the 288 open problems and the laws its census found. The Oracle indexes them as one
corpus (`oracleDocsFrom`, `oracleIndex`: BM25 over their own words in every language they carry — Russian, Greek and
LaTeX commands become words; a query word matches every word it begins) and answers with a dossier grouped by kind, each
item with its status stated (found, confirms, revises, tested; holds or fails as stated; open; a law of the census) and
the one action that reaches it. It returns only items of the atlas, never a sentence of its own. Humans: type `?question`
in the command palette (⌘K). Agents: `HCC_ORACLE.ask(question, {limit, perKind})` → `{query, words, indexed, complete,
total, top:[{kind,id,title,status,score,go}], byKind}`; `HCC_ORACLE.load()` fetches the formulas, problems and laws;
`HCC_ORACLE.open(question)` shows the dossier. Pure, so an agent can build the same index without a page:
`oracleDocsFrom({labs, discoveries, leads, relations, checks})`. Ledger `oracle` (tested). `docs/verify-the-oracle.cjs`.

**The tennis racket inside the fluid — every triad of S³ is a free rigid body (v4.345).** On the atlas's Galerkin
basis of S³ (Beltrami modes, curl e = μe, μ = σ(k+2)) the Lamb vector of two modes projected on a third is exactly
(μ_k − μ_j)·S_ijk·a_j a_k with S_ijk = ∫e_i·(e_j×e_k) totally antisymmetric (1e-15). Three modes alone therefore obey
Euler's equations of a free top with inverse moments 1/I = Sμ + c: energy Σa² is |L|², helicity Σμa² the kinetic
energy. Consequences, all measured: the middle SIGNED curl is the unstable axis (the Dzhanibekov/tennis-racket theorem
is Waleffe's instability, rate |S|A√((μ_hi−μ_mid)(μ_mid−μ_lo))); on the separatrix the unstable leg empties and its
energy splits (μ_hi−μ_mid) : (μ_mid−μ_lo) (1/8 : 7/8 for E₁₋E₂₊E₃₊); Jacobi's period 4K(m)/(g·max(p,q)) returns the
state to 1e-14. Which triads exist is a DOUBLE Clebsch–Gordan rule of Spin(4): E_{k,+} = ((k+2)/2, k/2),
E_{k,−} = (k/2, (k+2)/2), and a triad couples iff the left spins and the right spins each close a triangle (120 of 120
shell triples of the K = 3 basis agree with the numerics). Census to k = 12: 818 triads, 216 rotors, 322 forward, 280
split, none with its largest leg unstable, 72 extremal triads forbidden; every shell k ≥ 1 is the middle axis of
(E₁₋, E_k₊, E_{k+1}₊) and sends 1/(k+6) of its energy to the largest scale (shown in the FBS3R S³ tower). The crowd:
around one Beltrami mode the linearised fluid is A·S_J·D (S_J antisymmetric, D = diag(μ_c − μ_J)); one-sided blocks are
neutral (Arnold, Krein) — Killing fields and the top shell — while the whole fluid equals (E₂), tames (E₁, 0.037 vs
0.206) or amplifies (E₃ at K = 4, 0.266 vs 0.233) the best lone triad. Lab `triad` (energy sphere cut into orbits by
the helicity levels, the top turning, lever marks, a strobe at the exact period guarded by the display rate, spin
triangles for forbidden triads). Kernels: `triadCoeffs`, `triadPeriod`, `triadLever`, `triadBody`, `s3TriadAllowed`,
`s3TriadCensus`, `triadPick`, `triadCrowd`, `triadExperiment`. Tracks: `triad.top`, `triad.census`. Ledger
`triadRigidBody`, `racketLever`, `doubleClebschGordan` (resolves the lead spin-ns), `crowdAroundRacket`; new leads
`crowd-k`, `triad-closure`. `docs/verify-the-tennis-racket-inside-the-fluid.cjs`.

**The stroboscope of everything, the fluid first, the S³ spectrum on the φ-spheres, and an audit (v4.346).**

period P at time scale s turns s/(P·hz) per frame (true < ¼, ambiguous < ½, aliased above). A catalogue of 37 periods
with their kind and precision (`PHASE_CATALOGUE`, `phaseAll`), from the electron's Compton oscillation (8·10⁻²¹ s)
through atomic clocks, pulsars, sound, the day, the Moon, Jupiter's moons and the planets to Milankovitch, the galactic
year and the light's loop round S³ (~10²⁰ s), sits on one ladder of frequencies with the band the eye can follow
(`phaseWindow`) sliding along it; slow motion s = ε·P·hz (`phaseSlowMotion`), a strobe lock s = (N+ε)·P·hz
(`phaseStrobeLock`), Poincaré's section by flashing at A's period. Two phases on a torus T², three in a cube T³
coloured by the best integer relation (a resonance is a plane). Resonance finder: `phaseRelation2`/`phaseBestLock`

look-elsewhere factor), `phaseRelation3` (lattice |a|,|b|,|c| ≤ M, normalised by Σ|a|f), `phaseRelationNull` (random
log-uniform frequencies). Found blind: Laplace's f_Io − 3f_Europa + 2f_Ganymede = 0 (relative miss 9.3·10⁻¹¹, 0/300
random triples; strobed flashes on its plane to 10⁻⁷); Mercury's 3 : 2 locked within the data (p ≈ 4·10⁻⁴); the Venus
pentagram 8 : 13 (p ≈ 0.7) and Neptune–Pluto 2 : 3 (p ≈ 0.17) are what a continued fraction gives a random ratio.
Tracks `phase.relation`, `phase.lock`. FBS3R: the S³ spectrum is drawn on the φ-ladder's OWN nested spheres —
shell k at N_k = log_φ(2πR/((k+2)l_P)), radius φ^(N_k − D) round the bindu, Hopf circles, drift-ladder latitude rings,
exact triads as triangles (`fbsS3Pick`); the gap log_φ((k+3)/(k+2)) is 0.843 of a rung at k = 0 and under a quarter
from k = 6 — the spectrum is denser than the ladder everywhere. Audit (ledger `kernelAudit346`, revises): the

`spectrumOnLadder`, `kernelAudit346`. `docs/verify-the-stroboscope-of-everything.cjs`.

along the object's row and column (card, HUD, bars, coach bubbles all count), the picture slides into the largest open

**The universe is a resonator — global modes of S³ and the address of matter (v4.355).** A new laboratory
(`#/world/s3/lab/gmode`): if space is a three-sphere, every field on it is a sum of the sphere's own modes,
∇²Y = −k(k+2)Y/R² with (k+1)² modes in shell k, and a mode is a state of ALL of S³ at once. THE ADDRESS: the field of
shell k most concentrated on a point x₀ is the zonal kernel (k+1)U_k(x·x₀)/2π² — a Chebyshev polynomial of the 4-D dot
product (the addition theorem, equal to the sum over the Hopf-adapted basis cos^|p|η sin^|q|η P_n^(|q|,|p|)(cos 2η)
e^{i(pφ₁+qφ₂)} to 1e-15). Its lobe ends at ψ = π/(k+1), so πR/(k+1) → λ/2: the diffraction limit with no lens. THE
TWIN: U_k(−c) = (−1)^k U_k(c) — every single-shell address is exactly as loud at the antipode; one shell addresses
projective space, and a set of atoms closed under x → −x can be driven independently at no more than half of them.
THE CAPACITY: a beam f = Σa_j Z_k(·, x_j) solves G a = e; rank G ≤ (k+1)² (the 600-cell's 120 atoms saturate it up to
k = 5, never above their 60 antipodal pairs). LIGHT: for every holomorphic f of degree m, F = f(z)(ξ₂ + iξ₃) — ξ the
left-invariant frame, ξ₁ the Hopf (Reeb) field — has curl F = (m+2)F, div F = 0 and F·F = 0 (measured at random
points; ξ₂ − iξ₃ fails — only it kills holomorphic functions, the tangential Cauchy–Riemann equation). So
E + icB = F e^{−i(m+2)ct/R} is an exact null Maxwell field: E ⊥ B, |E| = c|B|, both in the contact planes, Poynting
exactly |f|²ξ₁ — the light's energy flows along the Hopf fibres, and z₁^a z₂^b lives on the Clifford torus |z₁|² = a/m,
with a stationary energy density (an eigenmode, not a soliton; a chiral subspace of dimension m+1 inside the
(m+1)(m+3)-dimensional eigenspace). No light below 2c/R (H¹(S³) = 0); 2(n²−1) modes at ω = nc/R,
(2n³+3n²−5n)/3 to shell n (Weyl). THE FISH-EYE: all light frequencies are integers in c/R, so a flash refocuses fully
at the antipode after πR/c and returns after 2πR/c — the closed universe (and the chart it is drawn in) is Maxwell's
fish-eye; with ω = √(k(k+2)) it disperses. MATTER: atoms (the 600-cell, clusters, antipodal pairs, or a crowd inside our
observable cap) glow with the steady excitation (Ω²/4)/(Δ² + Γ²/4 + Ω²/2) they take from the mode — frequency picks the
species, shape picks the place: global spectral addressing; tap an atom to address it. THE COSMOS (R = 548.3245 Gly,
the atlas's canonical modulus; the reconstruction's median and the curvature ledger are one tap away): the shells
k = 1, 2, 3 are 1989.10, 1218.07, 889.55 Gly; c/R = 5.78·10⁻²⁰ s⁻¹; the 21-cm line spans 5·10⁴ shells, Lyman α 10²⁸,
so no atom hears the discreteness unless coherent longer than R/c = 548 Gyr; the curvature Casimir energy 11ħc/120R
(ζ(−3) − ζ(−1) = 11/120, regularised here to 1e-9) is ~4·10⁻¹³⁰ of the dark energy. S³ gives discreteness and an
infrared scale, not a minimal length. API `gmode`, tracks `gmode.address`, `gmode.light`, `gmode.cosmos`,
