`unify.corrections`; ledger chiralSubspace, mirrorQuintic, specRecomputed; export `fbs3r_unified_fundamental_atlas.json`.
`docs/verify-the-unified-fundamental-atlas.cjs`.

**Knots of light — the null light of S³ in flat space (v4.357).** The resonator gains a mode "the same light in flat
space": Maxwell's equations are conformally invariant and Minkowski space is a patch of the Einstein cylinder R × S³
(T = atan(t+r) + atan(t−r), χ = atan(t+r) − atan(t−r)), so the null mode E + iB = P(z)(ξ₂ + iξ₃)e^{−i(m+2)T} pulled back
as a 2-form with the exact Jacobian (`gmodeFlatField`) is a finite-energy null Maxwell field in flat space — Gauss,
Faraday and Ampère hold by central differences to ~1e-7, E·B = 0 and |E| = |B| to 1e-16 (`gmodeFlatMaxwell`). For P = 1
it is Rañada's electromagnetic knot: its energy as a cloud, B lines (ice) and E lines (gold) traced live (one per
frame), closing on themselves; time runs through the knot's life in units of its conformal scale L — a mathematical
bridge (M08), not a cosmological claim. In the light mode the zeros of the light are drawn: P = 0 is a union of Hopf
fibres (z₁ = 0 for a > 0, z₂ = 0 for b > 0), violet vortex cores. Agents (Phase 8): `HCC_MECHANISMS.list/get/tiers/gates`
enumerate the 58 mechanisms and run the gates; `promote` refuses — a status changes only by review. The manifest
carries `unified_fundamental_atlas`. Track `gmode.flat`, ledger lightKnotsFlat. `docs/verify-the-knots-of-light.cjs`.

**The horizons follow the clock; the new laboratories in the headset (v4.358).** Reported: the light sphere did not
grow when the time machine ran, forward or back — every horizon had been built once, for today. They are now functions
of the cosmic time the clock shows (`hzAtT`): the atlas's ΛCDM + radiation chain integrated in ln a from the radiation
era into deep Λ domination, with an exact radiation start and Λ tail. The particle horizon (the observable universe)
shrinks to zero toward the Big Bang and grows toward χ_p(∞) = 62.4 Gly comoving; the event horizon χ_e = χ_p(∞) − χ_p
shrinks to a point, the Hubble sphere c/(aH) with it; the light-age, last-scattering, equality and acceleration screens
stand at χ_p(t) − χ_p(t_E) only after their events; before t = 0 nothing is drawn. Checked at the clock's extremes
(±2.4×10¹³ yr). The colour-of-time disc and its epoch rings now read each epoch on the observer's own past light cone,
χ_p(t) − χ_p(t_E) = χ — the old rule shifted every epoch by Δt, which is right only today (ledger horizonsInTime, a
correction; track `cosmic.horizons`). IN THE HEADSET: strokes of light measure their width against the eye's viewport and
clouds use an XR pixel scale (`hccPx`), so every S³ laboratory reads in a headset; the laboratory's numbers and its
instrument ride on a panel in front of the reader (the page HUD is not drawn in XR); a controller's trigger reaches the
resonator's atoms and the Unified Atlas's stars and gates (`HCC_RAY_TAPS`) before any teleport.
`docs/verify-the-horizons-follow-the-clock.cjs`, `docs/verify-the-laboratories-in-the-headset.cjs`.

**One model of the horizons for both worlds (v4.359).** Reported: flown out to the edge of Sun → Cosmos, the horizons
did not match the ones in Horizons — the solar chain kept its own Hubble sphere, event horizon and an "observable
universe" at a typed 46.5 Gly, while Horizons drew another set. Now there is one set (`HZ_GROUP`): ct, last scattering,
the particle horizon, the event horizon, acceleration onset, matter–radiation equality, the Hubble sphere c/(aH) (new in
Horizons, with its own switch) and the capacity horizon are built once, in Gly, and `cosmosHome` carries the SAME objects
into the solar chain's holder scaled exactly 1 Gly → GLY_AU when the Sun's world shows the cosmos (fills that would
paint over the sky stay off there) and back into Horizons otherwise. The solar duplicates are retired and kept only as
anchors of their waypoints, which stand at the chain's absolute radii. Every shell is scaled to value(t) / built radius
from `hzAtT` — no ratio to "today" remains, so a label and its shell cannot disagree, and the Horizons panel lists the
radii at the clock's time. Switching Sun → Cosmos → Horizons keeps the line of sight and maps AU → Gly, opening at
least at the outer framing where every horizon is in view. `docs/verify-one-model-of-the-horizons.cjs`.

**The causal calendar of the web; the web without cages; the CMB as the sky of every level (v4.360).** From one fact —
a radial light ray crosses comoving distance χ_p(t₂) − χ_p(t₁) between t₁ and t₂ — every catalogued structure now
carries a calendar on the clock (`hzCausal`, `HCC_CAUSAL`, track `cosmic.causal`, ledger causalCalendar): first light,
SUNSET t★ with χ_e(t★) = χ — at once the last moment a signal from here reaches it and the emission time of the last
event of it we will ever see — the arrival of a signal sent now, the return of its answer, and N = ⌊χ_e/2χ⌋ question–
answer exchanges left. A question is answered only from inside the DIALOGUE HORIZON χ_e/2 (8.17 Gly today, a new
shared shell that follows the clock); 151 exchanges remain with the Virgo cluster; the deadline to ask χ is the sunset
of 2χ; of the gas that made the CMB we see, only its first ≈ 0.74 Gyr will ever be seen. Every horizon card and the
Horizons milestone note are computed from the same chain (`hzCardRows`) — the event horizon card no longer quotes
16.68 Gly from another table. THE WEB WITHOUT CAGES: every extent drawn in the cosmic worlds (structure volumes in
both worlds, voids, local-web superclusters, Local Group surfaces, curvature and quantile families, the capacity
horizon) is a Fresnel limb (`hccGlassMat`) instead of a lat–long wireframe — the capacity horizon's cyan cage, carried
into the solar chain by v4.359, is gone; sightlines, the Shapley ⇄ Repeller axis and cones, the survey wedge, distance
spheres, the CF4 streamline sketch and containment lines are drawing aids, off by default and one switch away; the
galactic and dipole axes fade before the giant structures; structure centres are soft glows, not solid balls. The
observable ball in Horizons no longer holds 24 000 Math.random points around random centres: it holds the 5 959 VCV
quasars and 4 341 catalogued galaxies at their own directions and comoving distances. THE CMB AS THE SKY OF EVERY LEVEL: a switch in the solar
panel puts the relic radiation behind everything at every scale, riding the camera's rotation only, oriented exactly in
the IAU J2000 galactic frame; three ways to look — ℓ ≥ 2 anisotropy (the atlas's own ΛCDM realization, labelled as one),
as the Sun sees it with Planck's measured dipole (3362.08 μK toward l = 264.021°, b = 48.253°), and the colour it was
(`HCC_CMB_BACKDROP`). `docs/verify-the-causal-calendar.cjs`, `docs/verify-the-web-without-cages.cjs`.

**The real flow of the local universe (v4.361).** The continuity equation of the pressureless cosmic fluid — Euler
without pressure, the inviscid limit of the Navier–Stokes the S³ laboratories solve — is solved by FFT on the atlas's
own 17 300 measured redshifts (the band-pass local web, 64³ cells of 5.625 Mpc): v(k) = iβH₀θ(k)k/k², with Bernardeau's
spherical-collapse divergence θ(δ) = (3/2)[(1+δ)^{2/3} − 1] and β = 0.43 (2M++, Carrick et al. 2015), movable in the
panel (`webLinearFlow`, `HCC_WEB_FLOW`, track `web.flow`, ledger realLocalFlow, kind *tested*). The solver reproduces
the analytic infall onto a Gaussian lump to 2 % and obeys continuity and zero curl to 1e-14 on the real field. The
galaxies of the local web are drawn drifting along it (tracers start on catalogued galaxies; streak length is a stated
display scale). For the Milky Way it predicts ≈ 730 km/s toward l ≈ 149°, b ≈ 62° — 40° from Virgo, 79° from the
measured CMB motion of the Local Group — with 557 km/s toward Virgo against the measured 185 (β ≈ 0.14 would match):
the band-pass loses the Great Attractor and Shapley, and the compilation is denser in the north, so the direction
toward Virgo is the robust part and the amplitude awaits 2MRS and Cosmicflows-4 — whose hosts (CDS VizieR, EDD) this
build environment cannot reach. The observer and every galaxy pin are now marks of constant screen size: a 120-Mly
white ball no longer hides Virgo and the whole local web. `docs/verify-the-real-flow.cjs`.

**2MRS and Cosmicflows-4 in exact coordinates; the extents of every giant structure (v4.362).** The authoritative
CDS/VizieR files — 2MRS J/ApJS/199/26/table3 (Huchra et al. 2012) and Cosmicflows-4 J/ApJ/944/94/table2–4 (Tully et al.
2023) — are read by their ReadMe byte ranges and validated before embedding (`scripts/build-2mrs-cf4.mjs`, SHA-256
recorded): row counts 44 599 / 55 877 / 38 053, ranges, galactic against equatorial coordinates (four CF4-assigned PGC
900xxxx rows disagree by 0.26–0.92° and are kept on RA/Dec and listed by name), duplicates, CF4 Dist against its
distance modulus, table3/table4 order; 1 066 2MRS rows without cz are left out (43 533 placed). 2MRS stands in redshift
space (barycentric cz → CMB frame → comoving distance at the atlas's H₀ = 68.43); CF4 in distance space (measured
luminosity distance → comoving), its groups coloured by the published peculiar velocity. Measured here
(`surveyFluxDipole`, `surveyBulkFlow`, `surveyHubble`, `HCC_SURVEYS`, track `survey.bulkflow`, ledger surveysMeasured):
the 2MRS flux dipole points to l ≈ 256°, b ≈ 51°, 26° from the Local Group's CMB motion; the CF4 groups carry a bulk
flow of 202 ± 11 km/s toward l ≈ 288°, b ≈ 24° within 100–200 Mpc; the CF4 distance scale gives H₀ ≈ 75.8 against the
atlas's 68.43 — the Hubble tension, standing as a radial offset between the two layers. A switch in both worlds draws
every catalogued giant structure at its declared extent and orientation as a glass ellipsoid with a hairline 15°
graticule and a brighter equator, to read size and place by eye. `docs/verify-the-surveys.cjs`.

**The measured sky; every confirmed exoplanet (v4.363).** Planck 2018 SMICA (PR3, Nside 2048, from the Planck Legacy
Archive via IRSA; SHA-256 recorded, integrity checked against its own FITS header) is embedded by
`scripts/build-planck-sky.py` beside the atlas's own ΛCDM realization; both panels choose between them (`cmbSkySource`).
The last-scattering wall and the solar backdrop now read the map by exact Galactic direction (the wall used to read by
the sphere's ecliptic UVs — harmless for a realization, wrong for the measured sky). Measured on the map: the spectrum
outside the confidence mask is 1.019 × the atlas's CAMB for 30 ≤ ℓ ≤ 999 (1.10 above ℓ = 1000, where full-mission noise
is not subtracted); the Cold Spot found at l = 208.4°, b = −56.3°, −127 μK; the quadrupole and octopole axes 7.7° apart
near (240°, 56–63°); D₂ = 198 μK², a fifth of ΛCDM (ledger measuredCmbSky). Every confirmed exoplanet — 6 375 planets
around 4 780 stars from the NASA Exoplanet Archive (`scripts/build-exoplanets.mjs`, validated) — stands at its host's
direction and distance in the Sun's world, coloured by the star's temperature; the nearest and richest systems open with
their planets (`HCC_EXOPLANETS`). On the 3 178 transiting planets the radius valley is measured at 1.77 R⊕ between 1.60
and 2.47 R⊕ (`exoRadiusValley`, track `exo.valley`, ledger radiusValley). `docs/verify-the-real-sky.cjs`.

**The neighbourhood, the mergers, the slope (v4.364).** Gaia DR3 within 50 pc — 33 961 stars with parallax > 20 mas at
>10σ and RUWE < 1.4 from the ESA archive (`scripts/build-gaia-gw.mjs`, query and SHA-256 recorded) — stands in the Sun's
world at J2000 (positions carried from J2016.0 by proper motion) and MOVES on the atlas clock with each star's space
velocity (radial part where Gaia has one, flagged otherwise; straight lines, valid ~1 Myr). The 20 967 stars with 3D
velocities give the Sun U = 9.8, V = 21.0, W = 7.56 km/s relative to them (U, W as Schönrich 2010; V carries the
asymmetric drift) — `gaiaSolarMotion`, ledger sunAmongNeighbours. All 282 GWTC mergers with published distances and
masses (GWOSC, through GWTC-5.0) stand in Horizons as spheres of distance — the catalogue has no sky positions — and
GW170817 at NGC 4993; the primary masses peak near 11.5 and 38 M☉ (`gwMassPeaks`), the siren gives H₀ ≈ 75 (+45/−11)
from the median distance (ledger mergerPopulation). The radius valley on the Kepler planets alone is sloped, deepest for
R ∝ P^−0.10 (Van Eylen 2018: −0.09 ± 0.02) at 1.81 R⊕ for P = 10 d, and deepens under the geometric completeness weight
1/p_transit (`exoValleySlope`, ledger valleySlope). Track ops gaia.solarMotion, gw.massPeaks, exo.slope test each
estimator on a known answer. `docs/verify-the-neighbourhood.cjs`.

**Nothing under the clock, nothing on a panel (v4.365).** Reported: the time machine ate the lower edge of the windows
above it. Measured in a browser at 1024 × 700, 1280 × 800 and 1440 × 900: the controls panel and the hierarchy inset ran
37 px under the 51 px bar (the inset's --bottom-band rule was overridden by its later base rule, the controls had none,
and the inset's JS placement used the window's edge), the Info panel ran under it too, and with Info open the help button
and the First-Principles pill lay on its rows while the world caption ran under the Atlas Coach. Now one rule last in
the cascade stands every bottom-floating window on --bottom-band and clamps every top-hung panel to the room above the
bar; the inset floors on the bar and avoids it and the Coach; and a keep-clear pass moves right-pinned floaters left of
an open right panel and above the bar, the caption and each other, and narrows the caption to the free band. Zero
overlaps in the same states afterwards. `docs/verify-nothing-under-the-clock.cjs`.

**The stars on their true orbits (v4.366).** Reported: the Milky Way's stars stood still at full time-machine speed
while the disc wheeled past, and the Sun's circular track lay apart from both. The Gaia 50-pc layer moved on straight
lines frozen beyond ±1 Myr; every other layer rode Hill's linear epicycles, which a leapfrog integration in the same
Galaxy shows straying by 36 % of the distance in 100 Myr. Now every star — Gaia, Hipparcos, the named stars, the
nebulae and clusters, the arm tracers — rides its exact orbit in the axisymmetric Galaxy the atlas measures
(V_c = V₀(R/R₀)^β, β = 1 − 2A/Ω, vertical ν): `galTorus` finds the turning points from E and L, does one radial period
by spectral quadrature (R = c − a cos η) and keeps it as a table read by cubic Hermite interpolation starting at the
J2000 state; any epoch is the period count plus a point in the period (`galTorusAt`, `galOrbitAt`, `galRideOrbit`).
Agreement with the integration < 1 pc over ±2 Gyr, exact at J2000, E and L kept to 1e-5. The GPU evaluates 16-term
Fourier series of the same tori relative to the Sun (`gaiaOrbitAttrs`, `gaiaSunUniforms`, twin `gaiaOrbitAt`); the
~3 % plunging halo orbits it cannot follow move on the CPU. The Sun rides its own torus (8.10–9.34 kpc, radial period
182 Myr): the disc, its centre (`galCentreScene`) and the Sun's drawn track (its orbit one galactic year back and
ahead) all stand on it. Found in the embedded Gaia stars (`gaiaClosestPasses`): Gliese 710 passes at 0.052 pc in
1.29 Myr (Bailer-Jones et al. 2018: 0.052 pc, 1.28 Myr). Ledger trueOrbits, track op orbit.torus.
`docs/verify-the-true-orbits.cjs`.

**Reproducibility tracks — a discovery as a link anyone can replay.** A track (schema `hcc.track/1`, types in
`api/tracks.d.mts`) is where to stand (world, laboratory, camera), what to set, and which computations to run with
what they must return, serialised into a URL (`#track=` + base64url JSON). Opened in the atlas it replays step by step
and marks each expectation; `node api/track-replay.mjs '<link>'` runs the SAME calls on core/atlas/extracted.mjs
outside any browser. Calls may only name an operation of `TRACK_OPS` (15 pure kernels) with JSON arguments — a link
is data, never code. Thirteen ledger entries carry a canonical track (`HCC_TRACKS.discovery(id)`, the ⟲ button in the
Discovery Explorer); a fingerprint (FNV-1a of the canonical outputs) says whether two hosts computed the same numbers.
The first replay on two hosts caught the atlas disagreeing with itself: the page derives a dozen φ-ladder rows at load
from its own authorities, the core read the typed literals (and the extractor read `...GALAXIES` as member access);
both repaired, the φ-audit moved from Z = 1.855 to 2.048 on both hosts. `docs/verify-the-reproducibility-tracks.cjs`.

**Sketches.** Thirty-eight laboratories draw a chart — a curve, a bar, an axis — or next to nothing on the shared
backdrop; measured (the scene of every laboratory counted above the common S³ backdrop) and looked at, they are
grouped last as `sketch` ("a formula drawn, not yet a scene") in the browser, the lab bar, the XR menu and the palette,
so the laboratories that demonstrate are not diluted. Their numbers are exact; the list shrinks by rebuilding.

**The ghost sky — non-Euclidean optics of S³/Γ (space-form laboratory).** Light in S³ runs on great circles, so the
sky of S³/Γ is computed in closed form, not ray-marched: every catalogue structure q and its images g·q, each seen at
R·arccos(Re g·q) along its geodesic, at its own epoch, with angular size s/(R sin χ/R) (smallest a quarter of the way
round, growing beyond — the lens of a closed space). The observer's own images are the group: for the Poincaré space
12 Milky Ways at 36°·R, 20 at 60°, 12 at 72°, 30 at 90° … They enter the light horizon exactly when R < χ_LSS/θ_min =
71.8 Gly — half the radius (143.6) at which matched circles appear, so circles can exist in a universe whose ghosts
are all hidden, never the reverse. At R = 57 Gly: 1 148 ghost images inside the horizon, 12 of them the Milky Way, the
nearest 35.8 Gly away at z ≈ 20 — before the Galaxy formed. `docs/verify-the-ghost-sky.cjs`.

**From a coincidence to a hypothesis — `/ratio A : B`.** In the command palette (and `HCC_HYPOTHESIS.ratio(a, b)` for
agents): N = log_φ(A/B) and its distance δ to a rung (δ·ln φ is the precision the claim needs); the catalogue as its
own null — the fraction of all 6 328 pairs of scales as near a rung; the conventions nobody fixed by nature (radius ↔
diameter, π, 2π); and the falsification test it generates — do the two objects' families share the ladder's phase? —
run at once through the φ auditor. Proton radius / Bohr radius = φ^−22.961 (δ 0.039) is as near as 8% of all pairs and
dies under every change of convention: a property of how the lengths were defined. `docs/verify-the-hypothesis-engine.cjs`.

**The φ-ladder auditor.** Is ln R periodic with period ln φ? Two controls, both required. (1) Smoothed surrogates of
the catalogue itself — each ln R jittered by a Gaussian as wide as ln φ, which keeps every broader structure and
erases the ladder — with the look-elsewhere effect over every period 0.30–0.72, a tail extrapolation to 5σ, Morlet
windows along the ladder, and a Bayes factor (von Mises vs uniform, ln B = ln[(1/κ_max)∫I₀(κC)/I₀(κ)^K dκ])
calibrated on the same surrogates. (2) The rank of ln φ among the periods of the same data — because (1) erases every
structure narrower than ln φ, periodic or not. A planted ladder passes both (12.9σ, rank 0); narrow non-periodic
bands pass (1) at 6.4σ and fail (2), and are declared lumpy. The atlas's 113 literature scales (as the page reconciles
them): Z(ln φ) = 2.05, p = 0.13. The 5 959 quasars beat the smoothed catalogue at 6.2σ with ln φ at rank 43% — selection, not a ladder;
without the second control the auditor would have announced it. `HCC_PHI_CENSUS.audit(which)`.
`docs/verify-the-ladder-audit.cjs`.

**The Trisphere.** A laboratory that draws S³ whole — turned in R⁴ and projected
stereographically, with its Clifford tori and Hopf fibres — and places every laboratory on the
torus of its chain distance from the ten core stations, joined by geodesics of S³. Its
instrument returns the volume 2π²R³, the Clifford torus area, the Laplacian spectrum n(n+2)/R²
with multiplicity (n+1)² (= the harmonic polynomials, counted), and how many laboratories reach
S³. Every laboratory's S³ line has ⬡, which opens the Trisphere with that laboratory pinned and
its chain lit. `docs/verify-the-trisphere.cjs`.

**Open problems are published.** `/api/v1/open-problems` and `api/open-problems.json`
carry what this atlas knows it has not done, including defects found in its own
verifiers.

## Static, no browser required

    api/manifest.json        every laboratory, instrument and contract
    api/openapi.json         12 REST paths
    .well-known/mcp.json     9 MCP tools — list_labs, run_lab, sweep_lab, …
    api/sensitivity.json     every declared input swept, log-log slope fitted
    api/transfers.json       what actually moves along each coupling
    api/reach.json           what a control can reach, and how deep
    api/liveness.json        which views recompute per frame
    api/invariants.json      what every laboratory keeps, the law of each output, its symmetries, the laws across the bus
    api/open-problems.json   the unfinished list
    version.json             release identity

## Ground rules

Read `SCIENTIFIC_CONTRACT.md` before quoting a number as a prediction. The short
form: a value carries the class of the model that produced it, and an exact model
consequence is not an empirical forecast.
